input: Get an air quality monitor for the nursery

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Air quality monitors vary widely — some track only CO2, others cover VOCs, particulates (PM2.5), humidity, temperature, and more. Knowing which pollutants matter most determines which device to buy.
Whether the nursery is for a newborn, infant, or toddler affects sensitivity requirements and which health thresholds to prioritise.
Budget directly narrows the field — entry-level monitors cost ~$30, while comprehensive smart monitors can exceed $300.
The nursery's existing conditions (new construction, older home, urban vs. suburban) influence which pollutants are most likely present and worth monitoring.
Whether the user wants to buy online, in-store, or already has a brand in mind shapes the immediate next action.
Some users want a standalone display they can glance at; others prefer app-connected smart home integration — this affects which product fits their lifestyle.
Knowing whether 'done' means just having a reading device, or also acting on alerts (e.g., triggering a purifier), determines if the monitor needs smart/automation features.

gold.taskTitle: Get an air quality monitor for the nursery
gold.taskDescription: Source and set up an air quality monitor suitable for a nursery room, likely for a baby or young child.

questions.title: Which pollutants do you most want to track?
questions.description: Does the user want basic CO2/humidity, or a full suite including VOCs, PM2.5 particulates, and formaldehyde?

questions.title: How old is the child the nursery is for?
questions.description: A newborn vs. a toddler has different sensitivity levels and health thresholds to prioritise when choosing a monitor.

questions.title: What is your budget for this monitor?
questions.description: Budget narrows the product field significantly, from basic $30 sensors to comprehensive $300+ smart devices.

questions.title: Is the nursery in a newer build, older home, or urban area?
questions.description: The room's environment influences which pollutants are most likely present and worth monitoring.

questions.title: Do you prefer buying online or visiting a physical store?
questions.description: Determines the immediate purchasing path and whether to research shipping times or local availability.

questions.title: Do you want a screen display or app-based monitoring?
questions.description: Some users want a glanceable bedside display; others prefer smartphone alerts and smart home integration.

questions.title: Should the monitor connect to or trigger other smart devices?
questions.description: Knowing if the user wants automation — like activating a purifier on poor air quality — determines whether smart/integration features are required.
